chunks: Do not appropriate to yourself that in which the people have an equal share, nor be regardless of matters which have come to light with the excuse that you are accountable for others. Shortly, the curtains of all matters will be raised from your view and you will be required to render redress to the oppressed.

key_terms.أَغْطِيَةُ الْأُمُورِ: Curtains of matters (secrets or hidden truths)

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical warnings for governors in Imam Ali's letter to Malik al-Ashtar?
ai.summary: In this foundational text of Shia political ethics, Imam Ali instructs Malik al-Ashtar to avoid *al-isti'shar* (exclusively appropriating public wealth for oneself) and to cease feigning ignorance of evident matters, a warning rooted in the concept of *muhasaba* (accountability). This passage underscores the transient nature of worldly concealment, promising that divine justice will eventually uncover the leader's true conduct to vindicate the oppressed, a theme central to the Imamate's role as the guarantor of equity.
